hooks.text: A dead star is vaporizing its companion with particle beams.
A spinning dead star slowly vaporizes its partner into nothing.
A hyper-spinning neutron star blasts its mate with radiation daily.

title: The Dead Star Vaporizing Its Partner
description: Discover how a hyper-spinning black widow pulsar blasts its companion star with relativistic particle beams, slowly vaporizing it down to nothing.

beats.text: A dead star is vaporizing its companion with particle beams.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a black widow pulsar evaporating its companion star

beats.text: Most people think dead stars sit quietly in empty space.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a millisecond pulsar beaming radiation in space

beats.text: Instead, black widow systems feature a rapidly spinning millisecond pulsar.
beats.visual: diagram illustrating binary star system and Roche lobe deformation

beats.text: Old neutron stars spin up by siphoning matter from partner stars.
beats.visual: artist impression of matter transfer in a binary star system

beats.text: Intense radiation heats the facing side of the companion star.
beats.visual: artist concept of tidally locked star heated by pulsar radiation

beats.text: Gas blown off creates a plasma cloud that absorbs radio waves.
beats.visual: Chandra X-ray Observatory illustration of pulsar wind and bow shock

beats.text: Over millions of years, the pulsar vaporizes its mate into nothing.
beats.visual: artist impression of evaporating companion star in a black widow system

beats.text: That is how a dead star becomes a particle beam.
beats.visual: artist impression of a millisecond pulsar beaming radiation in space

better_than_last: Applied the myth_vs_fact structure precisely by contrasting the common belief about dead stars with the reality of black widow particle beam vaporization.
